label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: The restaurant is recognizable through left-side booths, repeated pedestal tables and chairs, pendant lamps, broad corner windows, ceiling strips, tiled floor and plants, though forms are simplified.

The author view retains booths on the left, tables and chairs through the center and right, windows across the back and right, and overhead pendants. Repetition is more regular and spacing more open than the target.
Tables, seating and ceiling clearance remain functionally plausible relative to one another. Chair backs and floor tiles are somewhat oversized, without destroying the overall scale relationship.
Light ceiling and tabletops contrast with darker seating, floor and pendant silhouettes. Boxy seating and simplified lamps preserve recognizable correspondence despite reduced material distinction.
The bright window perimeter and readable interior are broadly compatible with daytime illumination. Heavy noise and flat shading reduce quality but do not obscure the major content.
Complementary views reveal table thickness, chair backs and seats, pedestal supports and changing occlusion across a three-dimensional room.

Architecture, furniture and lamps have addressable mesh parts with finite nonempty geometry and assigned node materials. Actual parent chains connect these meshes to editable groups; this is supported beyond names alone.

dimension_scores.evidence: Major restaurant elements and their broad arrangement correspond, but the elevated author viewpoint, sparse plants, blank windows and primitive furniture substantially weaken resemblance.
Individual chairs and tables have visible pedestal supports and lamps have cords. Booth benches appear unsupported beneath their seats, and the plant occupies the same foreground area as a table.
Monochrome tonal organization is retained, but rigid slab furniture, square bases and flattened pendant bodies lack the reference silhouettes' refinement.
Severe render noise, uniformly simple surfaces, blank exterior panels and schematic vegetation produce an unfinished architectural blockout appearance.
Left booths, central circulation and right-side dining beneath pendants preserve the spatial identity. The furniture grid is more uniform and the room feels more elongated and sparse.
Furniture remains plausible against room height, but tall rectangular chair backs, broad booth tables and coarse floor divisions alter the target's relative proportions.
Bright perimeter lighting keeps geometry readable, while weak surface differentiation, featureless glazing and noisy soft shadows lose much of the target's depth.

Repeated seating, tables, pendants, architectural divisions and vegetation are present in substantial numbers. Plant density, exterior context and furniture construction details are considerably reduced.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
